```{r}
#get from input folder
#create output folder

input_folder <- "~/Desktop/research/Elton/CSVRaws"
output_folder <- "~/Desktop/research/Elton/timings"

#if (!dir.exists(output_folder)) {
 # dir.create(output_folder)
#}

csv_files <- list.files(path = input_folder,pattern = "\\.csv$",full.names = TRUE)

for (file in csv_files){
  df <- read.csv(file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  num_rows<- nrow(df)
  #if less than 80, skip
  
  if(num_rows < 80){
    message("skipping file because it has less than 80 rows") 
    next
  }
  
  #columns
  req_cols <- c("cuetype", "image.started", "getready.stopped")
  
  #should i write something to check if all the colums are there?
  
  cuetype <- df$cuetype
  image_started<- df$image.started
  getready_stopped<- df$getready.stopped[1]
  print(getready_stopped)
  
  #get new time
  time <- image_started - getready_stopped
  
  #new dataframe
  output_df <- data.frame(cue  = cuetype, time = time, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  
  #partID to name new file (i think)
  participant_id <- sub(
  pattern = "^(LARA[0-9]+).*",
  replacement = "\\1",
  x = tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(file))
)
  
  output_file <- file.path(output_folder, paste0(participant_id, "_timing.csv"))
  
  # Save it
  write.csv(output_df, output_file, row.names = FALSE)
  
}
```


```{r}
#thought i would give it a shot to separte the files by cuetype. this is that version.

#get from input folder
#create output folder

input_folder <- "~/Desktop/research/Elton/CSVRaws"
output_folder <- "~/Desktop/research/Elton/timingssorted"

if (!dir.exists(output_folder)) {
  dir.create(output_folder)
}

csv_files <- list.files(path = input_folder,pattern = "LARA.*\\.csv$",full.names = TRUE)
cue_types <- c("reward", "nonreward", "alcohol", "nonalcohol")


for (file in csv_files){
  df <- read.csv(file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  num_rows<- nrow(df)
  #if less than 80, skip
  
  if(num_rows < 80){
    message("skipping file because it has less than 80 rows") 
    next
  }
  
  #columns
  req_cols <- c("cuetype", "image.started", "getready.stopped")
  
  #should i write something to check if all the colums are there?
  
  #partID to name new file (i think)
  participant_id <- sub(
  pattern = "^(LARA[0-9]+).*",
  replacement = "\\1",
  x = tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(file))
)
  
  cuetype <- df$cuetype
  image_started<- df$image.started
  getready_stopped<- df$getready.stopped[1]
  print(getready_stopped)
  
  #get new time
  time <- image_started - getready_stopped
  
  #new dataframe
  output_df <- data.frame(cue  = cuetype, time = time, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  
  output_df$cue_clean <- tolower(trimws(output_df$cue))
  
  # makes one file per cue type
  for (cue_type in cue_types) {
    
    cue_df <- output_df[
      output_df$cue_clean == cue_type,
      c("cue", "time")
    ]
    
    output_file <- file.path(
      output_folder,
      paste0(participant_id, "_", cue_type, "_timing.csv")
    )
    
    write.csv(cue_df, output_file, row.names = FALSE)
    
    message("Saved ", cue_type, " timing file for ", participant_id)
  }
}

```
